answer: Forge-Bound Time Escrow: each identity must complete a physical work order—a forge task signed by a tamper-evident hardware token issued one-per-device at manufacture—and hold it idle through a randomized, publicly logged delay before the account activates. Duplicate tokens fail at sequential hardware attestation, so one operator cannot parallelize registrations. The floor cost is one physical device plus the idle time, multiplied across identities. Willow-signed audit logs expose recovery attempts; reef-like redundancy across independent verifiers blocks replay.
